_about: Every threshold the engine uses lives here with its source and verification status. Nothing is hard-coded in engine.py. 'verified' means the text was read at the listed source on the listed date. It does not mean a lawyer has confirmed how the rule applies to any project.

rules.label: Rolling stock domestic content threshold, by federal fiscal year of delivery
rules.verified_how: Statute read on Cornell LII (uscode.house.gov link failed). Same percentages confirmed on FTA's Buy America page.
rules.note: 49 CFR 661.11(a) on eCFR still reads 'more than 60 percent'. The regulation has not been amended to match the statute. The statute controls.

rules.label: Subcomponent share needed for a component to be of domestic origin uses the same percentage as the vehicle
rules.source: FTA policy notice, 81 FR 60278 (Sept. 1, 2016), sections III.C and IV.A; 49 CFR 661.11(g)
rules.verified_how: Federal Register text read on federalregister.gov.
rules.note: 49 CFR 661.11(g) itself still reads 'more that 60 percent'. FTA's policy applies 65 percent (FY2018-19) and 70 percent (FY2020 on). This is agency policy guidance, not regulation text.

rules.label: Which date picks the fiscal year
rules.verified_how: Notice read in part. It ties the percentage to vehicle delivery date, with special handling for options, piggybacks and older contracts that was not modeled.
rules.note: Every delivery from Oct. 1, 2019 on lands at 70 percent, so this only matters for old contracts.

rules.label: Final assembly of rolling stock must occur in the United States; final assembly labor is left out of component cost
US-manufactured component that fails the subcomponent test still counts its domestic subcomponents plus the cost of manufacturing the component
rules.note: The engine takes 'cost of manufacturing the component' as component cost minus the sum of listed subcomponent costs. Check that against the manufacturer's cost build-up.

rules.label: US-made subcomponent in a foreign-made component counts only if it re-enters under the tariff exemption in 19 CFR 10.11-10.24
rules.note: US raw materials exported into a foreign component are not subcomponents and do not count (661.11(k)).

rules.label: Average vehicle cost above which US steel or iron in a non-US frame or car shell is counted
FTA manufactured product: all manufacturing processes in the US and every component manufactured in the US. Subcomponent origin is ignored.
rules.verified_how: eCFR renderer API. FTA's Buy America page says the same.

rules.label: FTA steel and iron: all manufacturing processes in the US, except metallurgical processes involving refinement of steel additives
rules.note: Applies to construction materials made primarily of steel or iron. Does not apply to steel used as a component or subcomponent of a manufactured product or of rolling stock (661.5(c)).

rules.label: BABA manufactured product: manufactured in the US and cost of US components greater than this share of all component cost
rules.source: 2 CFR 184.3, definition of 'Produced in the United States', paragraph (2); cost rules in 2 CFR 184.5

rules.label: Part 184 does not apply to an existing Buy America preference that meets or exceeds BABA section 70914. For FTA-funded projects it mainly adds construction materials.
rules.source: 2 CFR 184.2(a); FTA Buy America page, 'Requirements for Construction Materials'
rules.note: FTA's page says Part 184 'largely does not affect FTA's existing standards for iron, steel, and manufactured products'. 'Largely' is FTA's word. Edge cases are for counsel.

rules.label: BABA iron or steel products: all manufacturing processes, from the initial melting stage through the application of coatings, in the US
rules.source: 2 CFR 184.3, definition of 'Produced in the United States', paragraph (1)

rules.label: An item is 'predominantly' iron or steel when iron and steel content exceeds this share of total component cost
rules.source: 2 CFR 184.3, definition of 'Predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both'
rules.note: Recorded for reference. The engine does not classify items. Category is an input.

rules.label: BABA construction materials and the 'all manufacturing processes' standard for each

value.non_ferrous_metals: From initial smelting or melting through final shaping, coating, and assembly (184.6(a)(1))
value.plastic_polymer: From initial combination of constituent plastic or polymer-based inputs until the item is in its final form (184.6(a)(2))
value.glass: From initial batching and melting of raw materials through annealing, cooling, and cutting (184.6(a)(3))
value.fiber_optic_cable: From initial ribboning (if applicable) through buffering, fiber stranding and jacketing; also the glass and optical fiber standards (184.6(a)(4))
value.optical_fiber: From initial preform fabrication through completion of the draw (184.6(a)(5))
value.lumber: From initial debarking through treatment and planing (184.6(a)(6))
value.drywall: From initial blending of mined or synthetic gypsum plaster and additives through cutting and drying of sandwiched panels (184.6(a)(7))
value.engineered_wood: From initial combination of constituent materials until the wood product is in its final form (184.6(a)(8))

rules.verified_how: eCFR renderer API. Standards are paraphrased closely; read the section for exact wording.

rules.label: Cement and cementitious materials, aggregates (stone, sand, gravel), and aggregate binding agents or additives are a separate category, not manufactured products or construction materials
rules.note: How FTA's own Part 661 treats these items was not researched. The engine reports them as 'review'.

rules.label: DOT public interest waiver for de minimis costs and small grants
rules.source: DOT waiver announced Aug. 16, 2023, as summarized on FTA's Buy America page
rules.verified_how: Only FTA's one-paragraph summary was read. The waiver notice itself, its scope (it may exclude rolling stock or iron and steel) and whether it is still in effect were not checked.
rules.note: The engine reports whether a project's non-compliant total fits inside these numbers. It never changes a FAIL to a PASS because of it.

rules.label: Post-delivery purchaser's requirements: resident inspector not required for these procurements
Pre-award audit complete before the contract is signed; post-delivery audit complete before title transfers
rules.note: Part 663 applies to rolling stock that carries passengers in revenue service (663.3).

rules.label: Buy Clean California Act applies to state agencies under the State Contract Act, UC Regents and CSU Trustees. Eligible materials: carbon steel rebar, flat glass, insulation, structural steel.
rules.note: A local transit district is not an 'awarding authority' under 3501(a). The check is off unless the project says its awarding authority is one of the three listed.

rules.label: Maximum acceptable global warming potential per eligible material
rules.source: Set by the Department of General Services under Cal. Pub. Contract Code 3502, published outside the statute
rules.verified_how: Not checked. The DGS limits were not read, so none are loaded.
rules.note: Add limits here as {material: {limit, unit}} after reading the current DGS table. Until then the engine reports 'limit not loaded' instead of guessing.
